cost_estimate: One additional batched quantization pass of B=8 per item; no codebook or recommender training cost change beyond the extra token vocabulary. Expected Stage2 wall time roughly 1.1–1.3x, dominated by quantization.
falsifiable_hypothesis: On held-out next-item evaluation, adding s_i improves Recall@K/NDCG@K over the same baseline SID, with the largest gain among items whose bootstrap agreement a_i is low; verify by overall metrics and predeclared agreement-bin slices. Reject if gains are absent or confined to one unstable random seed.
key_change: Generate several perturbed views of each training item embedding, quantize each with the trained codebooks, and append a small stability token to the ordinary SID. The token summarizes agreement, allowing the generative recommender to learn when a semantic code should be interpreted coarsely versus confidently.
motivation: Items with noisy, sparse, or ambiguous content embeddings can receive brittle codes; a recommender that treats these codes as equally certain may overfit accidental distinctions and miss useful alternatives.
novelty: Rather than changing the embedding geometry or adding another interaction-transition loss, measure how stable each item's quantized code is under train-only perturbations and expose that stability in its identifier.
risks: Embedding perturbations may not reflect real metadata noise; a stability token may just encode item frequency/popularity indirectly or consume sequence-model capacity. Hard agreement can be sensitive to sigma and codebook boundaries, and appended tokens may not be consumed usefully.

specification.text: For each item i with embedding x_i, form B train-only perturbations x_i^(b)=x_i+epsilon^(b), epsilon^(b)~N(0,sigma^2 diag(v)), where v is the per-dimension variance estimated over training-item embeddings. Quantize each view with the frozen baseline quantizer to obtain tuple q_i^(b). Let a_i=(1/B) max_q sum_b 1[q_i^(b)=q]. Assign stability token s_i= min(S-1, floor(S*a_i)), with S=4 bins (use bins [0,.5), [.5,.75), [.75,.95), [.95,1]); export SID_i=(q_i,s_i). Keep perturbations and all statistics fit using training items only; apply identical deterministic seeded perturbations at export. Compare against baseline at fixed sequence model and training budget.

title: Encode semantic-boundary uncertainty as an explicit SID token
